title: 1 Kings Chapter 14 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Kings chapter 14 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Kings Chapter 14 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Kings Chapter 14.

questions.question: Who fell sick at that time in 1 Kings 14?
questions.correctAnswer: Abijah, the son of Jeroboam
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 14:1 states that Abijah the son of Jeroboam fell sick.

questions.question: What did Jeroboam tell his wife to do before she went to see the prophet Ahijah?
options: Disguise herself so she would not be known as his wife
Bring a sacrifice for the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Disguise herself so she would not be known as his wife
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 14:2 shows Jeroboam instructing his wife to disguise herself so she would not be recognized as his wife.

questions.question: Where was the prophet Ahijah located when Jeroboam's wife went to see him?
questions.correctAnswer: Shiloh
questions.explanation: Jeroboam's wife was sent to Shiloh to find Ahijah, as stated in 1 Kings 14:2.

questions.question: What did Jeroboam's wife take with her to Ahijah?
options: Ten loaves, cracknels, and a cruse of honey
questions.correctAnswer: Ten loaves, cracknels, and a cruse of honey
questions.explanation: According to 1 Kings 14:3, Jeroboam’s wife took ten loaves, cracknels, and a cruse of honey to Ahijah.

questions.question: Why could Ahijah not see Jeroboam's wife when she arrived?
options: Because his eyes were set by reason of his age
Because it was dark inside the house
questions.correctAnswer: Because his eyes were set by reason of his age
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 14:4 explains that Ahijah could not see because his eyes were set by reason of his age.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD told Ahijah that Jeroboam's wife would pretend to be another woman when she came to him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 14:5 states that the LORD told Ahijah that Jeroboam’s wife would feign herself to be another woman.

questions.question: What did Ahijah say when he heard the sound of Jeroboam's wife's feet?
options: He said, 'Come in, thou wife of Jeroboam; why feignest thou thyself to be another?'
questions.correctAnswer: He said, 'Come in, thou wife of Jeroboam; why feignest thou thyself to be another?'
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 14:6 records Ahijah recognizing her and questioning why she pretended to be another woman.

questions.question: According to Ahijah, who exalted Jeroboam and made him prince over Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD God of Israel
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 14:7 states that the LORD God of Israel exalted Jeroboam and made him prince.

questions.question: True or False: Jeroboam was as faithful as David in keeping God's commandments and doing what was right.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 14:8 says Jeroboam was not as the servant David who kept God's commandments and followed Him with all his heart.

questions.question: What kind of evil did Jeroboam do according to Ahijah?
options: Made other gods and molten images to provoke God to anger
Built the temple of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Made other gods and molten images to provoke God to anger
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 14:9 states Jeroboam made other gods and molten images, provoking the LORD to anger.

questions.question: What consequence did the LORD say would come upon the house of Jeroboam?
options: He would cut off the remnant of Jeroboam's house as one takes away dung
They would build a great temple
They would be blessed with wealth
questions.correctAnswer: He would cut off the remnant of Jeroboam's house as one takes away dung
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 14:10 declares the LORD would bring evil and cut off the house of Jeroboam as one takes away dung until it is gone.

questions.question: True or False: Jeroboam's descendants who die in the city will be eaten by dogs, and those who die in the field will be eaten by birds.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 14:11 states that those who die in the city shall be eaten by dogs, and those in the field by fowls of the air.

questions.question: What was the fate of Jeroboam's sick son when Jeroboam's wife returned home?
options: The child died as soon as she entered the city
The child was taken to Shiloh
The child was hidden from the people
questions.correctAnswer: The child died as soon as she entered the city
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 14:12 and 14:17 tell that the child died when Jeroboam's wife came to the threshold of the door in Tirzah.

questions.question: In what order did these events occur in 1 Kings 14: Jeroboam's wife disguises herself, she goes to Ahijah, Ahijah delivers a message, Jeroboam's son dies. Which happened first?
questions.correctAnswer: Jeroboam's wife disguises herself
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 14:2-17 narrate the sequence starting with her disguising herself before going to Ahijah and then the son's death.

questions.question: True or False: Jeroboam's wife openly went to Ahijah without any attempt to hide her identity.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 14:2 and 14:5 show she was told to disguise herself and feigned to be another woman to hide her identity.

medium.title: 1 Kings Chapter 14 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Kings Chapter 14 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the LORD say would happen to Jeroboam’s child when Jeroboam's wife returned to the city?
options: The child would recover and live many years
The child would die upon her entering the city
The child would become king after Jeroboam
The child would be healed by the prophet Ahijah
questions.correctAnswer: The child would die upon her entering the city
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 14:12 states that when Jeroboam's wife enters the city, the child shall die. This is reiterated by the immediate fulfillment in verse 17.

questions.question: According to 1 Kings 14, why was Jeroboam’s child the only one of his house to be buried?
options: Because he was the eldest son
Because he alone showed some good toward the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Because he alone showed some good toward the LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 13 explains that the child was the only one of Jeroboam's house to be buried because some good was found in him toward the LORD, unlike the rest of his family.

questions.question: What does 1 Kings 14:14 indicate the LORD will do after the death of Jeroboam’s child?
options: Raise a king over Israel who will cut off Jeroboam’s house
Send a prophet to warn Israel
Bring peace between Israel and Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Raise a king over Israel who will cut off Jeroboam’s house
questions.explanation: Verse 14 states that the LORD will raise up a king who will cut off the house of Jeroboam, fulfilling the judgment against Jeroboam’s lineage.

questions.question: How does 1 Kings 14:15 describe the LORD’s punishment on Israel?
options: Israel will be smitten and scattered beyond the river
Israel will be given new land
questions.correctAnswer: Israel will be smitten and scattered beyond the river
questions.explanation: Verse 15 says the LORD will smite Israel like a shaken reed and scatter them beyond the river because of their idolatry and provoking the LORD to anger.

questions.question: What reason does 1 Kings 14:16 give for the LORD giving Israel up to their enemies?
options: Because of the sins of Jeroboam who caused Israel to sin
Because Israel did not build a temple
Because Israel worshipped the true God
questions.correctAnswer: Because of the sins of Jeroboam who caused Israel to sin
questions.explanation: Verse 16 clearly states that Israel is given up because of Jeroboam’s sins and how he caused Israel to sin, emphasizing the importance of leadership obedience to God.

questions.question: What happened immediately after Jeroboam’s wife arrived at the threshold of the door in Tirzah?
questions.correctAnswer: The child died
questions.explanation: Verse 17 reports that as soon as she came to the door at Tirzah, the child died, fulfilling the prophecy given by Ahijah in verse 12.

questions.question: How did all Israel respond to the death of Jeroboam’s child according to 1 Kings 14:18?
questions.correctAnswer: They mourned and buried him
questions.explanation: Verse 18 states that all Israel mourned for the child and buried him, in accordance with the word of the LORD spoken through Ahijah.

questions.question: According to 1 Kings 14:19-20, how long did Jeroboam reign, and who succeeded him?
questions.correctAnswer: Reigned 22 years; succeeded by Nadab
questions.explanation: Verse 20 states Jeroboam reigned 22 years and was succeeded by his son Nadab, showing the continuation of his dynasty despite the judgment on his house.

questions.question: What does 1 Kings 14:21 reveal about Rehoboam’s age and reign in Judah?
options: He was 41 years old and reigned 17 years
He was 30 years old and reigned 10 years
He was 50 years old and reigned 25 years
He was 20 years old and reigned 5 years
questions.correctAnswer: He was 41 years old and reigned 17 years
questions.explanation: Verse 21 states Rehoboam was 41 when he began to reign and ruled 17 years in Jerusalem, the city chosen by the LORD to place His name.

questions.question: What does 1 Kings 14:22 say about the behavior of Judah during Rehoboam’s reign?
options: Judah did good and pleased the LORD
Judah did evil and provoked the LORD to jealousy
Judah remained faithful to the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: Judah did evil and provoked the LORD to jealousy
questions.explanation: Verse 22 explains that Judah committed worse sins than their ancestors, provoking the LORD to jealousy, highlighting the importance of faithfulness.

questions.question: According to 1 Kings 14:23, what types of idolatrous practices were common in Judah under Rehoboam?
options: Building high places, images, and groves on hills and under trees
Offering sacrifices only at the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Building high places, images, and groves on hills and under trees
questions.explanation: Verse 23 describes how Judah built high places, images, and groves on hills and under trees, indicating widespread idolatry contrary to God’s commands.

questions.question: What is the significance of 1 Kings 14:24 mentioning sodomites in the land during Rehoboam’s reign?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 24 explicitly mentions sodomites in the land who practiced abominations like the nations the LORD had cast out, underscoring Judah's moral decline.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Kings 14:25-26, Shishak king of Egypt took away only the treasures of the king's house during his attack on Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verses 25-26 state that Shishak took away treasures from both the house of the LORD and the king's house, including all the gold shields Solomon had made.

questions.question: What does 1 Kings 14:27-28 describe about King Rehoboam’s response to the loss of the gold shields?
options: He made brass shields to replace them
He repented and sought the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: He made brass shields to replace them
questions.explanation: Verse 27 says that Rehoboam made brass shields instead of the gold ones and entrusted them to the chief of the guard, showing a practical but lesser response to the loss.

questions.question: What does the war mentioned in 1 Kings 14:30 indicate about the relationship between Rehoboam and Jeroboam?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 30 states there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam throughout their lives, reflecting ongoing conflict between Judah and Israel.

hard.title: 1 Kings Chapter 14 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Kings Chapter 14.

questions.question: What sinful practices are mentioned as being committed by Judah during Rehoboam's reign?
options: Building high places, images, groves; sodomy; abominations of other nations
Only building high places and groves
Keeping all the commandments of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Building high places, images, groves; sodomy; abominations of other nations
questions.explanation: Judah committed various sins including building high places, images, and groves, as well as sodomy and following abominations of the nations, as stated in 1 Kings 14:23-24.

questions.question: Who attacked Jerusalem in the fifth year of King Rehoboam's reign?
questions.correctAnswer: Shishak king of Egypt
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 14:25 records that Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem in Rehoboam's fifth year.

questions.question: What did Shishak king of Egypt take away from Jerusalem?
options: Treasures of the house of the LORD, the king's house, and all the shields of gold Solomon made
Only the gold shields of Solomon
questions.correctAnswer: Treasures of the house of the LORD, the king's house, and all the shields of gold Solomon made
questions.explanation: Verse 26 states that Shishak took the treasures of the LORD's house, the king's house, and all the golden shields made by Solomon.

questions.question: How did King Rehoboam respond to the loss of the gold shields taken by Shishak?
options: He made brass shields to replace them and put them in the hands of the chief guard
He made silver shields and placed them in the temple
He built a new treasury to store treasures
He sent envoys to Egypt to negotiate
questions.correctAnswer: He made brass shields to replace them and put them in the hands of the chief guard
questions.explanation: According to 1 Kings 14:27, Rehoboam made brass shields to replace the gold ones and entrusted them to the chief of the guard.

questions.question: What literary device is illustrated by the guard carrying the brass shields into the house of the LORD and then returning them to the guard chamber?
options: Inclusio, framing the narrative with repeated action
Chiasm, a mirrored structure of events
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio, framing the narrative with repeated action
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 14:28 describes the guard bearing the shields into the LORD's house and then returning them, an inclusio that frames this part of the narrative with symmetrical action, emphasizing the temple's diminished glory.

questions.question: What was the relationship between Rehoboam and Jeroboam during their reigns according to this chapter?
options: There was war between them all their days
They united Israel under one kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: There was war between them all their days
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 14:30 explicitly states that there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam throughout their reigns.

questions.question: Who succeeded Rehoboam as king of Judah?
questions.correctAnswer: Abijam, his son
questions.explanation: Verse 31 notes that after Rehoboam died, Abijam, his son, reigned in his stead.

questions.question: Which foreign queen is mentioned as Rehoboam's mother?
questions.correctAnswer: Naamah an Ammonitess
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 14:21 and 14:31 mention Rehoboam's mother as Naamah, an Ammonitess, indicating a foreign maternal lineage.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'groves' in 1 Kings 14:23 refers to what kind of objects or places?
options: Sacred wooden pillars or trees used in pagan worship
questions.correctAnswer: Sacred wooden pillars or trees used in pagan worship
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term 'Asherah' often translated as 'groves' refers to wooden poles or trees set up as objects of worship in pagan cults, as indicated in 1 Kings 14:23 and understood from Old Testament worship contexts.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage closely connects with the theme of foreign invasion and plundering in 1 Kings 14:25-26?
options: 2 Chronicles 12:1-9, which recounts Shishak's invasion of Judah
Exodus 12, describing the Passover and plundering of Egypt
Judges 6, the story of Gideon fighting Midianites
Isaiah 36, the Assyrian siege of Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: 2 Chronicles 12:1-9, which recounts Shishak's invasion of Judah
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 12:1-9 parallels 1 Kings 14:25-26 by describing Shishak's attack on Jerusalem and the plundering of treasures, providing a historical corroboration and expansion.

questions.question: The warning and judgment against Jeroboam's house in 1 Kings 14 foreshadow which later prophetic judgment against Israel?
options: The Assyrian exile described in 2 Kings 17
The destruction of Jerusalem by the Romans
questions.correctAnswer: The Assyrian exile described in 2 Kings 17
questions.explanation: The judgment on Jeroboam's house (1 Kings 14:10-16) foreshadows the eventual exile of Israel by Assyria recorded in 2 Kings 17, where Israel was uprooted for persistent sin.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Kings 14:22, Judah's sins were considered worse than those of their ancestors.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 14:22 states that Judah did evil above all their fathers had done, provoking the LORD to jealousy with their sins.

questions.question: True or False: Jeroboam's son Abijah was the only one of Jeroboam's house to be buried because some good was found in him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 14:13 states that only Abijah was buried because there was some good found toward the LORD in him, fulfilling the prophecy given by Ahijah.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of kings being judged for leading people into sin, as seen with Jeroboam in 1 Kings 14?
options: Romans 1:18-32, which discusses God's wrath against sinful leaders and nations
Matthew 5, the Sermon on the Mount
Revelation 21, the new heavens and new earth
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 1:18-32, which discusses God's wrath against sinful leaders and nations
questions.explanation: Romans 1:18-32 addresses God's righteous judgment against sinful rulers and nations, paralleling the judgment pronounced on Jeroboam's house in 1 Kings 14.

questions.question: How does the author of 1 Kings use the history of Jeroboam and Rehoboam to emphasize the theme of covenant faithfulness?
options: By contrasting their disobedience and its consequences with the ideal of David's faithful heart
By showing their military victories as signs of God's blessing
By focusing solely on their family lineage
questions.correctAnswer: By contrasting their disobedience and its consequences with the ideal of David's faithful heart
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 14:7-9 contrasts Jeroboam's evil deeds with David's faithful obedience, underscoring covenant faithfulness as the key measure of a king's success or failure.

theological.title: 1 Kings Chapter 14 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Kings Chapter 14 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated by God's ability to reveal Jeroboam's wife's disguised identity to Ahijah despite Ahijah's blindness?
questions.correctAnswer: Omniscience
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 14:4-6 shows that although Ahijah was physically blind, God revealed to him the true identity of Jeroboam's wife. This displays God's attribute of omniscience—His all-knowing nature.

questions.question: According to 1 Kings 14:9, what is the chief reason God pronounces judgment on Jeroboam's house?
options: Jeroboam made other gods and molten images, provoking God's anger
Jeroboam oppressed the poor and widows
Jeroboam broke the covenant with David
questions.correctAnswer: Jeroboam made other gods and molten images, provoking God's anger
questions.explanation: Verse 9 explicitly states that Jeroboam's sin was idolatry—making other gods and molten images—which provoked God to anger, leading to the judgment pronounced.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine judgment is taught by the prediction that the dogs and birds will consume Jeroboam's dead bodies?
options: The doctrine of God's righteous retribution
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of God's righteous retribution
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 14:11 shows a vivid image of divine retribution where the bodies of Jeroboam’s descendants will be desecrated, symbolizing God's just punishment for persistent sin.

questions.question: How does 1 Kings 14:14-15 contribute to the broader biblical narrative of exile and restoration?
options: It prophesies Israel's exile due to idolatry and God's scattering of His people
It promises immediate restoration after Jeroboam's death
It celebrates Israel's triumph over surrounding nations
It focuses solely on Jeroboam's personal fate without national consequences
questions.correctAnswer: It prophesies Israel's exile due to idolatry and God's scattering of His people
questions.explanation: These verses foresee the judgment of exile—God uprooting Israel from the land and scattering them beyond the river—due to their sins, connecting to the larger theme of exile and eventual restoration (cf. Deuteronomy 28:64).

questions.question: What theological insight about God’s sovereignty is revealed by the statement that God 'exalted' Jeroboam and 'rent the kingdom away from the house of David'?
options: God sovereignly appoints and removes rulers according to His will
God is limited by human political decisions
God always preserves the Davidic line unconditionally
God is indifferent to earthly kingdoms
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly appoints and removes rulers according to His will
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 14:7-8 reveals God's control over political authority, showing He raised Jeroboam and took away the kingdom from David’s house, emphasizing divine sovereignty.

questions.question: What does the death of Jeroboam's son upon the wife’s return to Tirzah signify in terms of divine justice and mercy?
options: God’s justice in punishing sin but mercy by allowing only one to die
God's mercy in sparing the entire family
God’s indifference to the sins of kings
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice in punishing sin but mercy by allowing only one to die
questions.explanation: Verses 17-18 show the child's death as a fulfillment of judgment, yet only this son dies because 'in him there is found some good thing toward the LORD' (v.13), indicating mercy within justice.

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed by His promise to 'raise up a king over Israel who shall cut off the house of Jeroboam'?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice in punishing sin
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 14:14 shows that God’s justice will be executed through a king raised to remove the sinful house of Jeroboam, reflecting divine righteousness.

questions.question: How do 1 Kings 14:22-24 reflect the theological problem of corporate sin in the kingdom of Judah?
options: The entire nation is guilty for continuing and exceeding past sins
Only the king is responsible for sin
Sin is only individual and not communal
Judah was completely faithful despite some sins
questions.correctAnswer: The entire nation is guilty for continuing and exceeding past sins
questions.explanation: These verses describe Judah doing evil beyond their fathers, building high places and images, showing corporate sin affecting the whole society and provoking God’s jealousy.

questions.question: What does the taking of treasures from the house of the LORD by Shishak signify about God’s judgment on Rehoboam’s kingdom?
options: God allows foreign powers to discipline His people for their sins
questions.correctAnswer: God allows foreign powers to discipline His people for their sins
questions.explanation: Verses 25-26 describe Shishak’s attack and looting, illustrating God’s judgment through foreign invasion due to Judah’s sins, consistent with Old Testament patterns of discipline (cf. 2 Chronicles 12:7).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that divine punishment described in 1 Kings 14 is unjust because it affects entire families and nations. What does 1 Kings 14:10-16 actually teach about the nature of divine justice and communal responsibility?
options: God’s judgment is just as it addresses both individual and corporate sin, showing the seriousness of covenant unfaithfulness
God punishes without reason or fairness
Only individuals suffer for their direct actions
Divine punishment is random and unrelated to sin
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment is just as it addresses both individual and corporate sin, showing the seriousness of covenant unfaithfulness
questions.explanation: Verses 10-16 illustrate that God’s judgment includes the house of Jeroboam and Israel collectively due to persistent sin and idolatry, affirming biblical teaching on communal responsibility and covenant faithfulness (cf. Ezekiel 18:20).

questions.question: What synthesis of doctrines about sin and divine providence emerges when considering Jeroboam’s rise and fall as described in 1 Kings 14:7-10 and 20-21?
options: God sovereignly raises rulers but holds them accountable for sin, which affects the nation’s fate
Human kings independently control their own destiny without divine involvement
Sin has no consequence in the divine plan
God’s providence protects sinful rulers indefinitely
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly raises rulers but holds them accountable for sin, which affects the nation’s fate
questions.explanation: Verse 7-10 explain God’s sovereign elevation of Jeroboam and subsequent judgment, while verses 20-21 show the continuation of kingship under divine oversight, combining sovereignty and moral accountability.

questions.question: How do the events of 1 Kings 14:30-31 illustrate the ongoing conflict between the divided kingdoms and its theological implications?
options: The persistent war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam reflects the consequences of disobedience and division in Israel
The kingdoms were united and peaceful throughout
The conflict was purely political with no spiritual significance
God ignored the division and conflict
questions.correctAnswer: The persistent war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam reflects the consequences of disobedience and division in Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 30 notes continuous war, highlighting the theological reality that division and sin lead to strife and judgment in God’s covenant people.

questions.question: What does the replacement of Solomon’s gold shields with brass ones by Rehoboam reveal about the nature of divine judgment and human response in 1 Kings 14:27-28?
options: It symbolizes loss of divine favor and a human attempt to maintain appearances amid judgment
It signifies improved wealth and prosperity
It indicates a cultural shift unrelated to divine judgment
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes loss of divine favor and a human attempt to maintain appearances amid judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 27-28 describe the replacement of precious gold with brass shields, reflecting the consequences of sin and judgment, while Rehoboam tries to uphold royal dignity despite loss.

questions.question: What combined theological teaching about God's faithfulness and human failure is conveyed by comparing Jeroboam's disobedience in 1 Kings 14:8-9 and Judah's sins in 14:22-24?
options: Despite God's faithfulness, both Israel and Judah repeatedly fail by turning to idolatry and abominations
God condones idolatry in both kingdoms
Only Israel sinned, Judah was righteous
Human failure does not affect God's covenant
questions.correctAnswer: Despite God's faithfulness, both Israel and Judah repeatedly fail by turning to idolatry and abominations
questions.explanation: Verses 8-9 and 22-24 show that both kingdoms abandoned God's commands, provoking His anger, despite His ongoing covenant faithfulness, illustrating human rebellion.

questions.question: What theological significance does the mourning and burial of Jeroboam’s son (1 Kings 14:18) have in the context of divine judgment?
options: It demonstrates that even in judgment, God's justice includes the dignity of death and communal grief
It proves that God is indifferent to human emotion
It shows that Jeroboam’s family was exempt from judgment
It indicates that death is the ultimate end without hope
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates that even in judgment, God's justice includes the dignity of death and communal grief
questions.explanation: Verse 18 records Israel mourning and burying the child according to God's word, showing respect for human dignity amid judgment, consistent with biblical views on death and community.
